long_biography.plain_text:
Peter Schaefer Price Jr. trained in molecular biology at the University of Wisconsin before earning an MBA at the University of Minnesota. He moved through Berlex Biosciences and merchant bank Burrill & Craves, then became president of PowderJect Vaccines. Under his leadership, the unit grew from a small research group into the world's sixth-largest vaccine company before its acquisition by Chiron. A subsequent stint at Bay City Capital added portfolio-company advice and investment due diligence to his operating experience.

In 2004, Price joined Pharmasset as president and chief executive. He directed the antiviral developer as three hepatitis C candidates advanced in clinical trials. When Gilead Sciences agreed to acquire Pharmasset for about $11 billion in 2011, Price's stock options and transaction-linked compensation converted a long biotechnology operating career into substantial personal wealth. The transaction closed the following year, ending his tenure at Pharmasset.
